about: Every assumption of PNR, each with its value, unit, source and status (CLAUDE.md R4, tested by app/src/config.test.ts). Status: OBSERVED measured · DERIVED computed from observations · MODELED our assumption, a correlation or a normative value · SIMULATED · MOCK.

alphaSlow.source: t-squared design fire, slow growth (1055 kW at 600 s). NFPA 72 Annex B; SFPE Handbook of Fire Protection Engineering, 5th ed., design fires

alphaMedium.source: t-squared design fire, medium growth (1055 kW at 300 s). NFPA 72 Annex B; SFPE Handbook, design fires

alphaFast.source: t-squared design fire, fast growth (1055 kW at 150 s). NFPA 72 Annex B; SFPE Handbook, design fires

alphaUltraFast.source: t-squared design fire, ultra-fast growth (1055 kW at 75 s), e.g. flammable liquids. NFPA 72 Annex B; SFPE Handbook, design fires

ventilationLimitKwPerM52.source: Ventilation-limited heat release Q = 1500·A·√H: Kawagoe (1958) air inflow 0.5·A·√H kg/s × ~3000 kJ per kg of air. SFPE Handbook, compartment fire chapters

mqhCoefficient.source: Hot-layer temperature rise ΔT = 6.85·(Q²/(A·√H·hk·AT))^(1/3): McCaffrey, Quintiere & Harkleroad (1981), Fire Technology 17(2):98-119. SFPE Handbook, Walton & Thomas, estimating temperatures in compartment fires

flashoverC.source: Flashover when the hot layer reaches 600 °C: the label used by NIST P-Flash (Tam et al.) and the common 500-600 °C upper-layer criterion (Drysdale, An Introduction to Fire Dynamics)

flashoverCriterion.source: Team choice: temperature matches the NIST training label; thomas = Q ≥ 7.8·AT + 378·A·√H (Thomas 1981, Fire and Materials 5(3):103-111)

thomasAreaKwPerM2.source: Thomas (1981) minimum heat release for flashover, wall-area term. SFPE Handbook

thomasVentKwPerM52.source: Thomas (1981) minimum heat release for flashover, ventilation term. SFPE Handbook

postFlashoverC.source: Hot-layer temperature held after flashover (fully developed fires reach roughly 900-1100 °C). Drysdale, An Introduction to Fire Dynamics, ch. 10

convectiveFraction.source: Convective share of the heat release in plume correlations. Heskestad, SFPE Handbook, fire plumes; NFPA 92

plumeK1.source: Plume mass flow above the flame m = 0.071·Qc^(1/3)·z^(5/3) + 0.0018·Qc. Heskestad, SFPE Handbook, fire plumes; NFPA 92 (2018) eq. 5.5.1.1

plumeK2.source: Same correlation, second term. NFPA 92 (2018) eq. 5.5.1.1

plumeFlameK.source: Plume mass flow within the flame, m = 0.032·Qc^(3/5)·z. NFPA 92 (2018) eq. 5.5.1.1a

flameHeightK.source: Mean flame height for a fire of unknown diameter, L = 0.166·Qc^(2/5). NFPA 92 (2018) eq. 5.5.1.1b

doorDischargeCoefficient.source: Discharge coefficient of a doorway for buoyant hot-gas outflow. Karlsson & Quintiere, Enclosure Fire Dynamics (2000), ch. 10; SFPE Handbook, vent flows

airCpKjPerKgK.source: Specific heat of air and smoke. Karlsson & Quintiere (2000)

rhoTKgKPerM3.source: Ideal gas: density × temperature of air at 1 atm. Karlsson & Quintiere (2000)

concreteConductivityWPerMK.source: Normal-weight concrete. SFPE Handbook, thermal properties of building materials; Karlsson & Quintiere (2000) table 6.1

gypsumConductivityWPerMK.source: Gypsum board, for light partitions. Karlsson & Quintiere (2000) table 6.1

gypsumThicknessM.source: Team assumption: one 16 mm board layer

leakageAreaM2PerM2Floor.source: Leakage of a room with every door closed, so a closed room still breathes a little. Team assumption, order of magnitude of NFPA 92 tight construction

doorJetFraction.source: Share of the excess fuel of a ventilation-limited room (free heat release above 1500·A·√H) that burns as a door jet in the next room, split by each open door's A·√H. Door jet fires as modelled in NIST CFAST (Peacock et al., CFAST technical reference guide)

spreadDelayS.source: After a flashover, a room joined by an open door ignites this long after. Team assumption (CLAUDE.md: spread through an open door after flashover)

doorFireResistanceS.source: A closed EI 30 fire door holds 30 min. EN 13501-2 classification

layerResponseS.source: Time constant with which the hot layer follows the quasi-steady MQH temperature (MQH has no thermal inertia of its own). Team assumption

ambientC.source: Indoor ambient temperature before the fire. Team assumption

failureC.source: A heat detector stops reporting above 150 °C, as assumed by NIST P-Flash (Tam et al. 2021)

noiseSdC.source: Reading noise, one standard deviation. Team assumption

rtiMs05.source: Response time index of a fixed-temperature heat detector (typical 25-100). SFPE Handbook, detector response

minGasVelocityMs.source: Gas velocity used for detector response outside the ceiling jet. Team assumption

alpertNearK.source: Ceiling-jet temperature near the plume, ΔT = 16.9·Q^(2/3)/H^(5/3) for r/H ≤ 0.18: Alpert (1972), Fire Technology 8(3):181-195

alpertFarK.source: Ceiling-jet temperature away from the plume, ΔT = 5.38·(Q/r)^(2/3)/H: Alpert (1972)

alpertTempRatio.source: r/H limit between Alpert's two temperature correlations: Alpert (1972)

alpertVelNearK.source: Ceiling-jet velocity near the plume, u = 0.96·(Q/H)^(1/3) for r/H ≤ 0.15: Alpert (1972)

alpertVelFarK.source: Ceiling-jet velocity away from the plume, u = 0.195·Q^(1/3)·H^(1/2)/r^(5/6): Alpert (1972)

alpertVelRatio.source: r/H limit between Alpert's two velocity correlations: Alpert (1972)

fsriRadiusM.source: Distance from the fire to a quadrant's thermocouple tree assumed when a UL FSRI ceiling thermocouple is turned into a detector signal (3.7 m room, quadrant centres about 0.9-1.9 m from the fuel). Team assumption

sampleS.source: Detector reporting period in the simulation (the training data step is checked when the NIST file is opened)

cylinderL.source: Water volume of a common 300 bar composite SCBA cylinder. Team assumption, to be validated with the Protection civile

startBar.source: Full cylinder pressure. Team assumption, to be validated with the Protection civile

whistleBar.source: Low-pressure warning of a self-contained breathing apparatus at 55 ± 5 bar: EN 137:2006

returnFactor.source: The way out is assumed 1.5× slower than planned (fatigue, smoke, a victim). Rule carried over from Martian Map's point of no return; team assumption

consumptionApproachLpm.source: Air use while advancing in smoke with equipment (training figures range 40-100 L/min by effort). Team assumption, to be validated with the Protection civile

consumptionWorkLpm.source: Air use while working at the objective (search, rescue). Team assumption, to be validated with the Protection civile

consumptionExitLpm.source: Air use on the way out. Team assumption, to be validated with the Protection civile

workAtObjectiveS.source: Default time spent at each objective. Team assumption

airLowCautionBar.source: Caution when the pressure drops below this. Team assumption

clearMs.source: Firefighter walking with breathing apparatus and equipment, no smoke. Team assumption, to be validated with the Protection civile

smokeMs.source: Advance in a smoke-filled room (reduced visibility). Team assumption, to be validated with the Protection civile

hotMs.source: Advance low in dense hot smoke, following a wall or a hose line. Team assumption, to be validated with the Protection civile

smokeAboveAmbientC.source: A room whose detectors read this much above ambient is treated as smoke-filled. Team rule (detectors only, R5)

hotC.source: A room whose detectors read this much is treated as hot dense smoke. Team rule (detectors only, R5)

doorPassS.source: Time to check and pass a door (door procedure). Team assumption

failedRoomCostMultiplier.source: Route cost multiplier in a room whose detectors have all failed (>150 °C at the ceiling): avoided, still crossable to get out. Team rule

predictedFlashoverCostMultiplier.source: Route cost multiplier in a room the model expects to flash over within 60 s. Team rule

fallbackThreshold.source: Decision threshold used only when ml/model/metrics.json gives none (the trained model's threshold is chosen for recall ≥ 0.95)

rerouteCostChange.source: Re-plan the route only when the verdict changes or its cost moves by more than this share (no flicker). Team choice

deadZoneWalls.source: A point is a radio dead zone when the straight line to the engine crosses at least this many concrete walls. Team rule, to be validated with the Protection civile

enduranceMin.source: Maximum flight time of a current industrial thermal drone (manufacturer spec sheet, 2022 enterprise class)

cruiseMs.source: Reconnaissance speed around the building. Team assumption (well below the class's 23 m/s maximum)

maxWindMs.source: Flight refused above this wind (the class is rated to 15 m/s; team margin)

batteryReservePct.source: Battery that must remain on landing back at the engine. Team assumption

thermalResolution.source: Thermal camera resolution of the class (manufacturer spec sheet)

climbMs.source: Climb and descent speed between the engine and the reconnaissance altitude. Team assumption (the class climbs at up to 6 m/s)

footprintM.source: Radius of ground seen by the thermal camera from 30 m (about 61° field of view). Team assumption

roofCoupling.source: Share of the hot-layer temperature rise seen on the roof by the thermal camera (simulated image). Team assumption

roofNoiseSdC.source: Noise of the simulated thermal image. Team assumption

loopOffsetM.source: Distance of the reconnaissance loop outside the building walls. Team assumption

plumeCoreRadiusM.source: No-fly disc around the fire, whatever the wind (thermal updraft). Team assumption

plumeExclusionLengthM.source: Length of the no-fly zone downwind of the fire. Team assumption

plumeExclusionHalfAngleDeg.source: Half-angle of the downwind no-fly cone. Team assumption

fuelLimitedShare.source: Share of generated fires limited by their fuel (growth, plateau, burnout) rather than by ventilation. Team assumption, added after the UL FSRI check showed the model treating every detector failure as a coming flashover; not fitted on FSRI

peakKwMin.source: Smallest peak of a fuel-limited fire (a wastebasket). SFPE Handbook, heat release rates of burning items

peakKwMax.source: Largest peak of a fuel-limited fire (an upholstered sofa). SFPE Handbook, heat release rates of furnishings; NIST Fire Calorimetry Database

plateauMinS.source: Shortest time a fuel-limited fire holds its peak. Team assumption

plateauMaxS.source: Longest time a fuel-limited fire holds its peak. Team assumption

decayS.source: Burnout time of a fuel-limited fire after its plateau. Team assumption

rapidPeakShare.source: Share of fuel-limited fires that reach their peak within seconds: flammable-liquid pool fires (the site's solvent store) and gas leaks. SFPE Handbook, pool fires

rapidPeakMinS.source: Shortest time to peak of a rapid fire. Team assumption

rapidPeakMaxS.source: Longest time to peak of a rapid fire. Team assumption

leakageFactorMax.source: Room leakage drawn log-uniformly between 1× and this many times fire.leakageAreaM2PerM2Floor: building airtightness varies by more than an order of magnitude (NFPA 92 leakage area ratios, tight to loose construction)

playbackSpeeds.source: Playback speeds offered; ×10 for the video. Team choice

seed.source: Random seed of the detector noise in the video scenario. Team choice

droneAtS.source: Simulated time at which the automatic demo launches the drone, once the detectors locate the fire. Video script, CLAUDE.md §9 step 2. Team choice

engageAtS.source: Simulated time at which the automatic demo engages the team (with the rehearsal: rehearses, then the COS validates the plan). Video script, CLAUDE.md §9 step 3. Team choice

indoorAtS.source: Simulated time at which the automatic demo sends the indoor drone in, just after the outdoor one: its flight lasts under 40 s, so that the rehearsal can start at engageAtS. Video script, CLAUDE.md §9 step 2b. Team choice

rehearsalHoldS.source: Wall-clock seconds the automatic demo holds the simulation while the rehearsal replays (rehearsal.playbackS) and the COS reads the plan: under 10 s, so that the video fits a minute. Team choice

closeDoorAfterNoGoS.source: Delay between the NO-GO and the COS closing the store-booth door in the automatic demo. Video script, CLAUDE.md §9 step 5. Team choice

reengageAfterOutS.source: Delay between the team being out and the PC re-engaging it on the remaining objective in the automatic demo. Video script, CLAUDE.md §9 step 6. Team choice

paceFastX.source: Playback speed of the automatic demo while nothing moves on the crew screens (fire growing, work at an objective), so that the demo lasts about a minute. Team choice

paceWalkX.source: Playback speed of the automatic demo while the team walks, slow enough to follow the view. Team choice

paceOutX.source: Playback speed of the automatic demo while the team is out and waiting for the PC. Team choice

arrivedM.source: Distance to its objective under which the team counts as working there (the demo then speeds up). Team choice

maxS.source: The automatic demo stops at this simulated time at the latest, whatever happens. Team choice

enduranceMin.source: Collision-tolerant indoor inspection drone class (protective cage), Elios 3 with its LiDAR and standard battery: 9 min (Elios 3 User Manual v1.3, section 2.4.3, p.23), 9.1 min (Elios 3 Technical Specifications v1.1, p.2). Without LiDAR 11.5 to 12.5 min; all in ideal conditions (sea level, 20 °C, new battery, hovering), so the lowest applicable figure is kept. Official documents read 2026-11-22, exact references in data/SOURCES.md. To validate by the Protection civile

cruiseMs.source: Elios 3 Technical Specifications v1.1, p.2: maximum horizontal speed 1.5 m/s in Assist mode (2 m/s Assist-Sport, 5 m/s Attitude, 7 m/s Sport). Assist is the mode that keeps the drone under its maximum collision speed of 2 m/s (User Manual v1.3, section 4.5.1, p.32), so we cruise at the Assist maximum. Exact references in data/SOURCES.md. To validate by the Protection civile

maxAmbientC.source: Elios 3 Technical Specifications v1.1, p.2: operating temperature 0 to 50 °C, valid for batteries pre-conditioned between 10 and 40 °C; confirmed as the maximum ambient temperature of the standard battery in every payload configuration (Elios 3 Batteries Technical Specifications, p.3). The drone does not enter a room whose detectors read this or more (the ceiling reads hotter than the drone's altitude: conservative). Exact references in data/SOURCES.md. To validate by the Protection civile

batteryReservePct.source: Same reserve policy as the outdoor drone (drone.batteryReservePct, R7): from every point the way home must still land with this reserve. Team rule

viewRadiusM.source: Distance, in clear line of sight, at which the thermal camera (160×120 px at 9 fps, Elios 3 Technical Specifications v1.1, p.3; field of view 56° × 42° of the same Lepton 3.5 module, Elios 2 RAD User Manual v1.2, p.16) tells a door's state, an obstructed passage or the heat behind an open door. Team assumption, to validate

thermalNoiseSdC.source: Standard deviation of the drone's room temperature reading (SIMULATED sensor noise). Team assumption

confidenceClear.source: Confidence of a drone observation taken in clear air (thermal and visible camera). Team assumption, to validate

confidenceSmoke.source: Confidence of an observation taken in smoke: the visible camera sees nothing, only the thermal one counts. Lower than in clear air. Team assumption, to validate

confidenceHalfLifeS.source: Time over which an observation's confidence halves: a fire changes a room within a minute or two. Team assumption, to validate

confidenceExpiry.source: Below this confidence an observation has expired and its room is UNKNOWN again (R10). Team assumption

unknownCostMultiplier.source: Route-cost multiplier of a room nobody has observed since the drone flew: an absence of observation is never a proof of safety (R9), so it is never free. Team assumption, to validate

observedHotCostMultiplier.source: Route-cost multiplier of a room the drone saw at or above progression.hotC. Team assumption

tooHotCostMultiplier.source: Route-cost multiplier of a room too hot for the drone to enter (« trop chaud pour le drone » is itself an observation that makes things worse, R9). Team assumption

contactDelayS.source: Time a team loses when it meets a passage the plan does not show (a collapsed rack): it stops, sizes it up, reports it by radio and waits for the new route, all at working effort. Team assumption, to validate with the Protection civile

flashoverMarginS.source: A room becomes impassable in the rehearsal this long before the flashover the AI predicts for it. Safety margin, team assumption, to validate with the Protection civile

playbackS.source: Wall-clock duration of the rehearsal replay in the self-playing demo (at ×20 the whole sequence must stay under 10 s). Team choice
